title: Autonomic Playbook Compiler for Ops Helper Utilities
creator: Ravi Kapoor
description:
Goal: Build a compiler that turns operational runbooks (human-written playbooks) into taskified, idempotent microservices (tasklets) that can be executed via the admin CLI or the ops API with safe dry-run and replay capabilities.

Scope: input is our canonical runbook DSL (YAML/annotated Markdown). Output artifacts: (1) a validated tasklet manifest (JSON schema) with typed inputs, permissions scope, and telemetry hooks; (2) a small runtime shim (Go) that enforces idempotency markers and auditing; (3) an admin CLI command scaffold for dry-run, simulate, and apply.

Why: current runbooks are freeform and require manual translation to runnable actions. Engineering and oncall time is lost to repeated manual steps and implicit knowledge. Compiling playbooks reduces human error, improves observability, and enables safe automation and replay.

Design decisions and trade-offs (summary):
- Compile-time validation vs runtime checks: prefer aggressive compile-time validation (input schema generation, permissions linting) to keep runtime shim minimal and low-latency. This increases upfront UX work for runbook authors but reduces incident blast radius.
- Idempotency strategy: use operation tokens + step-level checkpoints persisted in a small metadata store (Postgres) rather than complex distributed transactions. This keeps the shim simple and recoverable across restarts.
- Permissions model: generate least-privilege IAM policy snippets per tasklet and require an ops-approved policy before enabling auto-run. For Dedicated/Private customers, allow KMS-wrapped secrets for sensitive steps.
- Telemetry: include structured event emission (compact envelope) for each step with trace_id, step_name, latency_ms, outcome. Integrate with existing Datadog dashboard (link below).

MVP scope for this ticket: prototype compiler CLI, schema generation for three common runbook patterns (service-restart, cache-warm, failover-to-backup), runtime shim with dry-run and apply modes, integration test harness and basic telemetry.

Acceptance criteria:
- CLI can convert a DSL playbook into tasklet manifest and stub runtime in one command.
- Generated manifest includes typed inputs (JSON schema), required scopes, and telemetry hooks.
- Dry-run mode simulates steps without making destructive calls and produces a replayable trace artifact.
- Integration tests for the three patterns pass in CI.
- Security review checklist completed and KMS integration validated in a staging run.

Notes on risks and mitigations:
- Risk: incorrect permission generation could allow over-broad actions. Mitigation: require manual policy approval gate in console before enabling auto-run; CI lint job to flag wide-scoped policies.
- Risk: state store becomes a single point of failure. Mitigation: design metadata store for simple leader election and use DB-backed checkpoints with retry semantics; fall back to conservative manual steps if store is unreachable.

Links and artifacts:
- Design doc (Confluence): https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/INFR/pages/7891012/Autonomic+Playbook+Compiler
- Prototype PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/ops-playbooks/pull/312
- Datadog dashboard (telemetry): https://app.datadoghq.com/dashboard/redwood/runbook-compiler-metrics
- Example DSLs and manifests: https://drive.redwood.ai/ops-playbooks/examples.zip

Next steps (implementation plan):
1) Finalize manifest schema and publish spec (this ticket).
2) Implement CLI parse->validate->emit pipeline and run internal authoring workshop.
3) Build runtime shim with idempotency and telemetry hooks.
4) Wire up CI integration tests and the security review flow.
5) Pilot with one SRE team, gather m-retro and iterate.
